key_insight: VoxProg turns natural-language instructions for placing objects in 3D scenes into executable programs over local voxel representations. This gives language models a concrete way to express spatial relationships that instructions leave implicit.
problem_solved: Placing objects correctly in 3D requires translating vague spatial language into geometric references grounded in scene surfaces.
method: Represent local regions of scene surfaces using voxel views.
Use a language model to interpret placement instructions and generate programs operating on these views.
Express geometric references and placement logic as executable code.
impact: VoxProg offers practitioners a program-based approach to connecting language understanding with 3D geometry. The provided abstract is truncated, so benchmark results and performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: spatial instruction → language model → voxel program → 3D object placement.

paper_title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
paper_authors: Zhichao Zhai, Menglei Zhao, Guikun Chen, Zihao Yan, Kanzhi Wu
